headline: Warm, dry weather through Friday, then cooler with light rain Saturday and early next week.
summary: A ridge of high pressure, a zone of settled, sinking air, is parked over the Northwest, giving us a warm, mostly dry stretch through Friday. Highs reach the 70s, with the mid 70s on Friday, and people especially sensitive to heat may feel it. Morning fog or low cloud is possible Thursday. Winds turn easterly and gusty in the Cascades and foothills Thursday night. The ridge weakens over the weekend as a trough, a dip in the jet stream, moves in. Saturday brings light rain, mostly to the North Cascades, while the Seattle area may stay dry, and highs fall to the low 60s. Sunday is cooler and drier, with chilly lows in the 40s around Puget Sound and 30s in the foothills. Cool, unsettled weather with occasional light rain lingers into early next week, with the best chance on Tuesday. Forecasters say the pattern after that is unclear.
changes: The morning discussions expected showers on Saturday, focused near the King/Snohomish county line, and a second system Sunday and Monday that was forecast to miss Washington. The later discussions describe a weaker Saturday system that may leave the Seattle area dry, and Sunday lows that are a bit milder than earlier projected.
